lines.text: To read, not for to read!
Many learners say: I use my phone for to read.
Better: I use my phone to read.
To shows the reason. No for.
To! I use my phone to read.

data.wrong: I use my phone for to read.
data.right: I use my phone to read.
data.why: To shows the reason. No for.

native.tip: En español “para leer” se traduce solo con “to read”: no hace falta “for.”

en.hook: “For to read”? Do not say it!
en.tip: Spanish “para leer” is just “to read” in English, with no “for.”
en.caption: Many learners say “I use my phone for to read.” Spanish “para leer” is just “to read” in English, with no “for”: “I use my phone to read.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
